gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the two makers' Thunderbolt numbers on one scale. UGREEN advertises a '40Gbps link' and QNAP prints '20 Gbps Thunderbolt networking', but Liliputing found Windows reporting the UGREEN DXP480T Plus Thunderbolt network link at 20/20 Gbps, the same ceiling QNAP states. Measured on a Mac, every published figure is for a QNAP: 2,252 MB/s on the TS-h966TX (QNAP's lab) and 1,929 MB/s on the TBS-h574TX (StorageReview). No named reviewer has published a Mac-over-Thunderbolt number for any UGREEN.
standout_why: Compared against the cited QNAP US pages for the TVS-h674T, TVS-h874T and TBS-h574TX, UGREEN's Thunderbolt how-to blog, and ChatGPT's answers. QNAP's pages give only QNAP's 20 Gbps cap. UGREEN's blog gives only 'Thunderbolt 4 provides a 40Gbps link' plus rough per-drive MB/s ranges it says are not UGREEN results. ChatGPT repeated QNAP's 20 Gbps and implied UGREEN is a cheaper equal, without saying the UGREEN link also runs at 20 Gbps. Liliputing appeared once, uncited, at rank 30 in one chat, so the 20/20 Gbps reading was in a result but no page set it beside QNAP's figure. The TBS-h574TX product page also does not say that its own 1,393/1,410 MB/s figure came from a Windows Server 2019 PC, not a Mac. It shows the client only in the test notes.
decides: It removes '40 Gbps' as a reason to pick UGREEN: both brands deliver one 20 Gbps-class IP link per cable, so the real difference is price and storage, not link speed. For a shopper who needs Mac numbers they can check, QNAP is the only brand with published Mac-over-Thunderbolt figures: TS-h966TX 2,252 MB/s write (QNAP's lab, MacBook Pro M4 Pro) and TBS-h574TX 1,929 MB/s write (StorageReview, M1 Max). The UGREEN DXP480T Plus at $849.99 is still the value pick. Its only published Thunderbolt figure is 1.51 GB/s from an Intel NUC, so on a Mac it should be described as unmeasured.

findings.label: Maker's Thunderbolt figure (networking cap, not port rate)
findings.value: 20 Gbps maximum Thunderbolt networking bandwidth; 2× Thunderbolt 4; requires macOS 13.5 or later
findings.source_title: TVS-h674T | Thunderbolt 4 NAS. Designed for creators and small studios | QNAP (US)
findings.note: Quote: 'adopts Thunderbolt Networking technology and provides maximum bandwidth of 20 Gbps.' The page gives no MB/s transfer figure for Thunderbolt.

findings.label: Thunderbolt ports and host limits (hardware spec)
findings.value: 2 Thunderbolt 4 ports, delivered by a Thunderbolt 4 card preinstalled in PCIe slot 2 (Gen 4 x4); limited to Windows/Mac hosts and USB storage; third-party Thunderbolt external storage not supported
findings.note: The spec page gives no Gbps rate for the ports. The Thunderbolt card takes one of the two PCIe slots, leaving the x16 slot for a 10GbE card.

findings.label: Maker's own Thunderbolt throughput, and the test client behind it
findings.value: 1,393 MB/s write, 1,410 MB/s read, 1 direct-connected client, measured on a Windows Server 2019 PC (i9-12900E), not a Mac; 5× 3.84 TB E1.S RAID 5, QuTS hero h5.2.3
findings.note: The same page states 'Thunderbolt Networking for peer-to-peer connection, up to 20Gbps' and 'macOS 13.5 (or later)'. StorageReview (2024) quoted QNAP's launch figure as 1,637 MB/s write and 1,736 MB/s read, so the maker's own number has dropped since launch.

findings.label: Measured over Thunderbolt from a Mac (named reviewer)
findings.value: 1,929 MB/s write, about 1,850 MB/s read (ATTO, QD8, 4 threads, M1 Max MacBook Pro)
findings.source_title: QNAP TBS-h574TX Thunderbolt 4 NAS Review, StorageReview (Vince Carnevale, 2024-04-02)
findings.note: 1,929 MB/s × 8 = 15.4 Gbps. The reviewer says it 'fully saturated the 20Gbps connection the Thunderbolt network offers.' A Windows 10 PC with a Thunderbolt 3 add-in card managed 1,650 MB/s write but only 70 MB/s read.

findings.label: Maker-measured Thunderbolt throughput on a Mac
findings.value: 2,252 MB/s write, 2,004 MB/s read (AJA, 16 GB 5K RED pattern, MacBook Pro M4 Pro, macOS 26.0, 4× PM9A3 U.2 RAID 5)
findings.note: 2,252 × 8 = 18.0 Gbps, about 90% of the page's stated '20Gbps throughput'. QNAP's own lab test, not an independent review. The page also says 'Direct-connect features are fully validated for Intel and AMD-powered USB4 / Thunderbolt 4 systems.' Core i3 6-core, 5× 3.5-inch SATA + 4× U.2.

findings.label: Maker's Thunderbolt figure (port rate, not networking cap)
findings.value: 'Thunderbolt 4 provides a 40Gbps link'; needs UGOS 1.2.0.2121 or later; one computer per port; the two ports are not bonded; SMB over a dedicated Thunderbolt IP address
findings.source_title: How to Connect UGREEN NAS via Thunderbolt 4 (UGREEN)
findings.note: Lists the DXP480T Plus, DXP6800 Pro and DXP8800 Plus as supported. Its MB/s figures (HDD 200–260, SATA SSD 500–550, NVMe over 1 GB/s) are, in its words, 'practical reference ranges', not UGREEN test results. Unlike QNAP, it names no minimum macOS version. The page date prints as 10/01/2025, ambiguous between January and October.

findings.label: Negotiated Thunderbolt network link and measured copy (named reviewer, PC client)
findings.value: Windows reported the link as 20/20 Gbps (other PCs ranged from 10/10 to 20/20). 100 GB copy: 1.51 GB/s (12.08 Gbps) receiving, 1.42 GB/s (11.36 Gbps) sending, Intel NUC 13 Extreme
findings.source_title: UGREEN NASync DXP480T Plus Review, Liliputing (Ian W Morrison, 2024-09-10)
findings.note: This is the key finding: UGREEN's '40Gbps' becomes a 20 Gbps IP link in practice, the same class as QNAP's stated cap. The best unnamed PC reached 2,464 MB/s sequential read in CrystalDiskMark. No Mac was tested.

findings.source_title: UGREEN NASync DXP480T Plus (UGREEN US store)

findings.source_title: UGREEN NASync DXP8800 Plus (UGREEN US store)

findings.label: Thunderbolt link on a Mac is a network share, not a disk
findings.value: Even over the Thunderbolt cable the TVS-h874T is reached 'as a network drive' at a Thunderbolt IP address
findings.source_title: Qnap TVS-h874T review: NAS & DAS all in one, ITdaily (Michaël Aussems, 2025-11-28)
findings.note: ITdaily published no Thunderbolt MB/s figure for the h674T/h874T.

findings.label: Thunderbolt direct-connect requirements (maker FAQ)
findings.value: Works only from a Thunderbolt 3/4/5 or full-featured USB4 host port with a certified cable; macOS 'recommended for better transfer efficiency'; the Thunderbolt IP may change after a restart
findings.source_title: Thunderbolt direct connect, TerraMaster Help Center
findings.note: The FAQ names no models and gives no speed figure.

unsourced: A Mac-client Thunderbolt throughput figure from a named reviewer for any UGREEN model (DXP480T Plus, DXP6800 Pro, DXP8800 Plus). StorageReview tested only over SMB/CIFS, Notebookcheck did not test Thunderbolt, and the only Mac number I found was a Reddit owner's post, which does not meet the sourcing rule.
Any measured Thunderbolt MB/s for the QNAP TVS-h674T or TVS-h874T. The QNAP product and spec pages and ITdaily's review give none.

The TerraMaster F6-425 Pro product page and datasheet, where search snippets show a 40 Gbps port claim and '10-20 Gbps' bridge throughput. terra-master.com returned 429, the datasheet PDF and forum labeling notice returned 403, so this is not verified.
Wording on the UGREEN DXP480T Plus product page (port rate, footnotes). WebFetch returned 429 twice.
Whether the new UGREEN DXP6800 Ultra ($1,449.99 on the US store) has Thunderbolt and is supported for direct connection. Its page returned 429.
